newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GOODWIN HOMER IN 12TH GIVES REDS WIN OVER CUBS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GOODWIN HOMER IN 12TH GIVES REDS WIN OVER CUBS.

text.p: Curtis Goodwin's first home run in nearly two years, a three-run shot with one out in the bottom of the 12th inning, gave the Cincinnati Reds a 4-1 victory over the Chicago Cubs Saturday.

The Reds denied the Cubs a season-high third straight win by holding them to seven hits and a walk with 15 strikeouts. Jeff Shaw (1-0) pitched three scoreless innings and gave up three hits with four strikeouts to get the victory.

Turk Wendell (2-3) took the loss when Goodwin golfed the first pitch he saw over the wall in right field for his first homer since July 1, 1995, when he was with the Orioles. It was his first National League homer.
"I don't think it can get any more exciting than that," Goodwin said. "I was just looking for something to hit."
Eddie Taubensee hit a one-out homer in the bottom of the ninth to tie the game 1-1 for the Reds.
"It felt good to get one when it counted," said Taubensee, who was 1-for-7 with four strikeouts against Mel Rojas before the homer.
With two out in the fourth, Sammy Sosa ripped his 12th homer an estimated 441 feet over the centre-field fence.

Then in the ninth, against Stan Belinda, Sosa hit what was initially ruled a home run down the left-field line, but third-base umpire Frank Pulli asked for help from home-plate umpire Greg Bonin, who ruled the ball foul.
"The last time I saw the ball, it was fair," Pulli said. "I lost it in the lights, I screwed up. My partner made the right call."
Television replays revealed it was the correct call, but Cubs manager Jim Riggleman argued vehemently and was ejected.
"To be honest, when he hit it, I didn't think it would be fair. Then I thought it was fair -- that's why I argued," Riggleman explained.
"I talked to some people since then, and some said it was fair and some said it was foul. It was probably foul. The umpires have to get the call right and I guess they did."
In Philadelphia, Bernard Gilkey, Butch Huskey and Carlos Baerga each drove in two runs and Armando Reynoso (3-0) pitched seven strong innings as the New York Mets beat the Phillies 8-4.

Gilkey, coming out of a season-long slump, had a sacrifice fly in the first to put the Mets ahead to stay and a solo homer off starter Calvin Maduro (3-6) in the fourth. Over his last nine games, Gilkey is 10-for-29 (.345) with three homers and six RBI to raise his average to .208.
Huskey hit a two-run homer.
At Colorado, Darryl Kile, Russ Springer and Billy Wagner combined on a four-hitter and Jeff Bagwell homered and scored three times as the Houston Astros beat the Rockies 7-0.

Kile (5-2), despite a 43-minute rain delay that followed the fifth inning, gave up four hits and walked three with five strikeouts in seven innings. He lowered his ERA to 1.88. He is 4-0 this month with a 0.47 ERA in five starts.

In Los Angeles, Raul Mondesi and Billy Ashley homered in a five-run first inning against Tom Glavine (5-3), and Eric Karros added a three-run blast as the Dodgers pounded the Atlanta Braves 10-3 to snap a six-game losing streak.
Ramon Martinez (4-3) tossed a three-hitter for his first complete game of the season, helping the Dodgers end their longest skid since 1992. It also broke Atlanta's seven-game winning streak.
Martinez did not allow a hit after Ryan Klesko's two-out homer in the fourth, retiring 16 of the last 19 batters.

In Montreal, Jeff Juden had a season-high seven strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings for his 10th straight win and rookie Vladimir Guerrero had a career-high four RBI as the Expos defeated the Pittsburgh Pirates 7-3.
Juden (5-0) allowed three runs and six hits with four walks as Montreal won for the eighth time in its last 10 home games. Juden has not lost since September 10, 1995 when he was with the Phillies.

In San Diego, Moises Alou and Bobby Bonilla each had three hits, including run-scoring singles in a three-run eighth inning, as the Florida Marlins overcame a five-run deficit and beat the Padres 9-7.
Florida banged out 17 hits.
The Padres had their winning streak snapped at a season-high five games.

In San Francisco, Andy Benes struck out a season-high 12 batters in seven innings and Ray Lankford drove in four runs as the St Louis Cardinals won for just the second time in eight games, 9-3 over the Giants.
Benes (3-2) gave up two runs and five hits with two walks.
Ron Gant and Mike Difelice each posted career highs with four hits for the Cardinals, who improved the National League's worst road record to 7-18.
